uncited: This family defines the differentiable rendering pipelines that convert a set of 3D Gaussian primitives (or their variants) into 2D images by projecting them onto the camera plane and compositing them.
It solves the problem of efficiently rasterizing soft, view-dependent primitives while supporting inverse rendering tasks such as lighting estimation and physical parameter optimization.

What sets these methods apart from standard rasterization is the use of alpha blending or weighted-sum compositing over sorted or spatially hashed primitives, often augmented with volume-based occlusion or explicit geometric intersection for sharp features.
All methods in this family share the core mechanism of projecting 3D primitives into 2D screen space and accumulating color based on depth order or spatial locality.
**Projection:** Primitives are transformed from world space to camera space.
**Rasterization:** Primitives are assigned to screen tiles.
Visibility is determined by bounding boxes or projected extents.
**Compositing:** Color is accumulated using front-to-back alpha blending or order-independent techniques.
The rendering pipeline relies on efficient rasterization of 2D Gaussians projected from 3D.
Subsequent works have adapted this pipeline for differentiable rendering, volume lighting, and physical parameter estimation.
